brief: Custom-fit leather handbags, Italian-made, handcrafted in Florence. Minimum order ships in 6 weeks. Average price point $1,200.

profile.brief: Custom-fit leather handbags, Italian-made, handcrafted in Florence. Minimum order ships in 6 weeks. Average price point $1,200.
profile.business_summary: A Florence-based brand selling handcrafted, custom-fit Italian leather handbags at around $1,200, made to order with a 6-week lead time.

picks.name: The Sustainability Buyer

avoid: Vague eco claims or unsubstantiated 'sustainable' labels
Fast-fashion comparisons that imply seasonal turnover
picks.ad_angle: Nothing is made until you order it — one bag, one maker, zero deadstock.

creative.angle: A commissioned milestone gift, planned six weeks ahead
creative.headline: A gift you commission, not buy
creative.body: Handcrafted in Florence, custom-fit to one person. Made to order and ships in six weeks, so plan the occasion early.
creative.offer_suggestion: Complimentary gift presentation box and a dated gift card confirming the commission for the recipient to open on the day
creative.tone_notes: Leads with the commissioned-gift framing rather than luxury self-treat, so it differs from the classic and sustainability cards. Treats the six-week lead time as part of the gesture instead of hiding it, which suits conservative high-AOV apparel placements. No urgency, no fast-shipping promise, no subscription language, and price is left out of the copy since this shopper isn't price-led.

plan.summary: No placement earns core budget at a $1,200, 6-week-lead-time price point against baskets under $200, so the plan is three tests on affluent women's apparel and footwear checkouts (Marlowe & Co., Linden Park, and Stride & Stem moved up for the shoes-to-handbag accessory moment), with everything else excluded on price or purchase-moment mismatch.

test.name: Stride & Stem
test.tier_reason: Scored 35 mainly on a values mismatch, but the purchase moment is a real accessories adjacency the tag map underweights: a high-income professional woman who just bought work shoes is shopping her outfit, and a handbag is the companion accessory. Audience (94% female, 28-48, high income) is the right buyer for a $1,200 bag.
test.rationale: "Professional women" buying women's shoes at $142 are assembling a work wardrobe, and a custom leather handbag is the standard next accessory; worth measuring whether craftsmanship framing lands on this audience.

evidence.quote: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate

test.risk: The notes say sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate — this audience may read $1,200 Italian leather as the opposite of what it buys, and the price is 8.5× the typical basket.

test.name: Marlowe & Co.
test.rationale: Notes say "Older affluent women" who respond to "quality messaging" — the closest thing in the catalog to a made-in-Florence craftsmanship pitch, and a handbag is the natural accessory next to the workwear/casual pieces just bought.

evidence.quote: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging

test.risk: $1,200 is ~10× the $112 typical basket and the notes flag "Lower impulse", so a 6-week made-to-order commitment may need several impressions before any conversion.

test.name: Linden Park
test.rationale: Highest-AOV apparel audience (50-70, 98% female, high income) buying classic workwear — a heritage Italian leather handbag is a credible next accessory purchase for that wardrobe.

evidence.quote: Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog. Conservative brand sensibility

test.risk: $128 basket vs $1,200 offer, and the "Conservative brand sensibility" audience may be loyal to established designer labels rather than an unbranded custom maker.

launch_summary.summary: The entire $10,000 runs as a test, split evenly across three affluent women's apparel and footwear checkouts — Marlowe & Co., Linden Park and Stride & Stem — at $3,333.33 each, because no publisher's shoppers clearly match a $1,200 made-to-order handbag. Each placement is measuring whether craftsmanship and heritage framing converts against baskets of roughly $112 to $142, with 14 days to hit a $360.00 cost per new customer before being promoted or cut. Expect exploratory results: about 28 conversions estimated in total.
uncertainties: The $360.00 target is 30% of the stated $1,200 first order, but real margin and repeat purchase value aren't known, so the whole payback assumption could be off.
All three placements sell items around ten times cheaper than the handbag, and a 6-week custom-fit commitment may need more exposure than a single post-checkout impression allows.
The buyer being a woman aged 30-60 and buying one time rather than repeatedly are both assumed, which shapes targeting and the bid.
questions: What is your actual margin on a $1,200 bag, and do customers ever order again?
Who actually buys — is the 30-60 female assumption right, and how often is the buyer purchasing as a gift?
Do you have geographic or income data on past customers that would narrow the US-Northeast, South and West targeting?
